title: Verifier Verdict Contract
description: Machine-checkable form of a mandatory verifier's output. Severity grammar, the mandatory closing verdict, and the summary line are grounded verbatim in conductor/review-output-standards.md ('Severity-Tiered Output Format', 'Mandatory Closing Verdict', 'Review Summary Line'). The primary-artifacts-only requirement and the six named verifiers are grounded in conductor/verification-routing.md ('Routing Table', 'Verifier Brief Standard'). review-output-standards.md defines THREE distinct per-role closing-verdict vocabularies (Quinn/Reid: BLOCK | APPROVE WITH SUGGESTIONS | APPROVE; Cyra: BLOCK | CONDITIONAL PASS | CLEAR; Leah: HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW confidence, no disposition at all). This schema normalizes all three onto one canonical `disposition` axis (BLOCK | APPROVE_WITH_SUGGESTIONS | APPROVE) so a single ship-gate check works across every verifier, and preserves the agent's literal wording in `role_verdict_raw` for traceability. Mapping: CLEAR -> APPROVE, CONDITIONAL PASS -> APPROVE_WITH_SUGGESTIONS, BLOCK -> BLOCK; Leah's confidence tiers are a separate, non-disposition axis carried in `confidence`. Phase 0 / Design Decision #3.

verifier.description: verification-routing.md Routing Table — the six named mandatory verifiers.

output_domain.description: verification-routing.md Routing Table column 1, e.g. 'Code diff / PR', 'Security', 'Research / intelligence claims'.

primary_artifacts_read.description: verification-routing.md: 'the diff, the logs, the URLs, the file paths — never Tess's summary of those artifacts. A verifier that reads the orchestrator's summary inherits the orchestrator's confabulations and verifies nothing.' Required non-empty so a verdict cannot exist without at least one primary artifact the verifier claims to have read itself.

findings.description: review-output-standards.md 'Severity-Tiered Output Format': every finding is [SEVERITY] area/file:line — finding — risk — fix/action.

severity_counts.description: Must match the actual tally of findings[] by severity — checked as a lint rule by tessctl validate (review-output-standards.md 'Review Summary Line': 'Found [N] CRITICAL, [N] HIGH, [N] MEDIUM, [N] LOW').

summary_line.description: review-output-standards.md 'Review Summary Line', e.g. 'Reviewed [scope]. Found [N] CRITICAL, [N] HIGH, [N] MEDIUM, [N] LOW. Top priority: [description].'

disposition.description: Canonical closing verdict, normalized from review-output-standards.md's per-role grammar (see top-level description).

role_verdict_raw.description: The verifier's literal per-role wording, e.g. 'CLEAR', 'CONDITIONAL PASS', 'Confidence: HIGH' — preserved for traceability back to review-output-standards.md's exact vocabulary.

confidence.description: Leah's confidence axis (research/intelligence verdicts) — a separate axis from disposition, not a substitute for it. review-output-standards.md 'Leah (Research & Intelligence)' section.

accepted_high_findings.description: H2 FIX (Fable adversarial review, BLOCK finding): the explicit-acceptance escape hatch review-output-standards.md's severity table implies for HIGH ('blocks approval' — unlike CRITICAL's unconditional block, HIGH is a strong default, not an absolute) but Phase 0 had no mechanical field for. A HIGH-containing verdict may only carry a non-BLOCK disposition if this array names, by `location`, every HIGH finding being knowingly shipped and WHY. It is never a blanket flag — see the per-finding `allOf` rule below, which requires every HIGH finding's location to have its own entry. Not available at all for Cyra (security) verdicts: see the no-escape `allOf` rule.

covers_paths.description: Phase 2 addition (ULTIMATE_FRAMEWORK_PLAN.md Design Decision #6 — 'the ship-gate refuses pushes... without a covering APPROVE verdict'). Repo-relative path globs (`**`-aware, same matcher as `tess.manifest.json`'s `owned_globs` / `core/policy/policy.yaml`'s rule globs) this verdict's review actually covered — i.e. `primary_artifacts_read` scoped to what a ship-gate can match against a diff. OPTIONAL and purely additive: existing verdict instances written before Phase 2 remain schema-valid without it. `tessctl gate`'s covering-verdict check treats a verdict with no `covers_paths` (or an empty array) as covering NOTHING — fail-closed by omission, not fail-open — so a pre-Phase-2 verdict never silently 'covers' a path its author never scoped it to.

then.$comment: review-output-standards.md severity table: CRITICAL 'Must be fixed before merge/deploy. Blocks approval.' A verdict cannot declare a CRITICAL finding and a non-BLOCK disposition — this is the schema check that makes 'tests pass, ship it' impossible to cash when a CRITICAL finding is present.

allOf.$comment: H2 FIX, security no-escape rule: review-output-standards.md's Cyra (security) section treats a HIGH-severity security finding with the same must-block weight review-output-standards.md gives CRITICAL elsewhere — security holes do not get an 'accepted risk' shortcut through this contract. A Cyra verdict with ANY HIGH finding must disposition BLOCK, full stop; `accepted_high_findings` cannot move a Cyra verdict off BLOCK (contrast the next rule, which is the only place the acceptance field has teeth).

H2 FIX (closes the BLOCK finding): 'a verdict with a HIGH finding + disposition: APPROVE currently passes' — before this rule there was no gate at all on that combination. review-output-standards.md's severity table gives HIGH 'blocks approval' as the default; this rule makes that default mechanical for every non-security verifier: a HIGH finding forces BLOCK unless `accepted_high_findings` carries at least one explicit, rationale-bearing acceptance. (Cyra is excluded here because the rule above already forces Cyra to BLOCK unconditionally — the two rules are mutually exclusive by `verifier` enum.) `_lint_verdict` in tessctl additionally checks every HIGH finding's `location` has its own acceptance entry, not just one entry covering all of them.

location.description: Must match the `location` of the specific findings[] entry (severity HIGH) being explicitly accepted.

rationale.description: Why shipping with this specific HIGH finding open is a deliberate, reasoned call — not a default.

$comment: Minimal-validator keyword subset supported by tessctl validate: type, enum, const, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, if/then/else, oneOf, anyOf, allOf, contains, $ref, $defs.
